rows.text: The device is signed out of your account. The other person will see they are signed out the next time they open a Google app.
The app will no longer get your mail, and if the other person uses it, they may notice your mail stops arriving.
The app stops getting your location. The other person may notice when your location stops updating.
Google may still send codes to your old phone number for 7 days after you've changed it. The other person may notice this happening and could potentially use those codes during that time.
Google may still send verification codes to your old email for 7 days after you change it. The other person may notice this and could potentially use a code before it stops working.
The other person may notice that the prompts stop showing up on their removed phone. Google might also still send codes to that phone for 7 days.
Sam may notice when you disappear from their map, and the arrival/departure alerts they set stop working.
The link stops showing where the other person is. The company's page doesn't say if anyone is told. The other person may notice when it stops working.
New mail no longer goes to the other person's Gmail address. They may notice if forwarded messages stop arriving.
The matching mail will no longer go to the other person's address. They may notice it stops working.

The hidden mail starts appearing in your inbox.
The other person would only notice if they look at your filters or your inbox.
The other person can no longer open your mail and will notice the next time they try. Gmail's page doesn't say if the other person is told about this change.
Sam will lose access to shared benefits and content when they shop or watch. They may notice when these are no longer available.
Riley may notice when they can no longer shop from your account, as they will no longer be able to make purchases.
Sam may notice when your account’s content stops showing on their Echo Dot.
Sam may notice when purchases you shared through the family group stop working for them.
Google sends Riley an email saying Riley was removed.
The other person can no longer see the photos you shared. They may notice when they look at them again.
The other person may notice when the device is signed out of your account next time they open a Google app.
The app stops getting your mail, and if the other person uses it, they may notice your mail stops arriving. The company's page does not say if the other person is told.
The app stops getting your location, and if they use it, they may notice your location stops updating. The company's page does not say whether the other person is told.

Google may continue to send verification codes to the old phone number for 7 days after you change it. The other person may notice if codes are still being sent there, and they could still use those codes during that time.
Google may still send codes to your old email for 7 days after you make changes.• The other person may notice if they read those codes.
Google may continue to send verification codes to the removed phone for 7 days. The other person might notice the prompts stop, or they could still receive a code during that time.
Sam may notice when you disappear from their map, and any alerts they had for you will stop working.
The link will no longer show your location. The other person may notice when they open the link after 9:00 PM.
The other person will no longer receive new mail forwarded to their address. They may notice that copies stop arriving.
The matching mail stops going to the other person's address. Gmail's page doesn't say if the other person is told, but they may notice the forwards stop working.
The hidden mail will start appearing in your inbox. Whoever created the filter will notice if they look at your filters or your inbox.
The other person can no longer open your mail and will notice the next time they try. The Google page doesn't say if they are told about this change.
Sam will notice when they can't access the things you shared, like if they try to shop or watch something. They will still have their own account.
Riley may notice that they can no longer shop from your account. This is because removing them disconnects them from your Family account and they lose access to shared benefits.
The Echo Dot stops showing your account's content. If Sam uses the Echo Dot, Sam will notice it’s not connected to your account anymore.
Sam may notice when the purchases you shared stop working for them. The family group list is still available to them.
Google sends Riley an email saying they were removed.
The other person may notice when you remove them. They will no longer be able to see the photos you shared with them.
The device shows that you are signed out of your account. The other person will see a "Signed out" indication the next time they open a Google app on that device.
The app stops getting your mail, so if the other person uses it, they may notice your mail stops coming in.
TrailMate may notice when your location stops updating. The app can’t get your location anymore if it doesn't have access to your Google Account.

When you change your recovery phone number, Google may still send codes to the old number for 7 days. The other person may notice if codes are sent to that number, and they could still use a code during that time.
The other person might notice if Google still sends codes to your old email for 7 days after you change it. They could still use a code during that time.
The other person may notice that prompts stop appearing on their removed sign-in phone. Google might still send codes to that phone for 7 days.
Sam may notice when you disappear from their map, and any alerts they set for your arrival or departure will stop working.
The link stops showing where the other person is. The company's page does not say if the other person is told. The other person may notice when the link stops working.
New mail will no longer go to the other person's address. The Gmail page does not say if Gmail tells them, but they may notice the forwarded copies stop arriving.
The matching mail stops going to their address. The company's page does not say whether Gmail tells the other person when this happens, but they may notice that it stops working.

The hidden mail starts appearing in your inbox.
The other person would only notice if they look at your filters or inbox.

The other person can no longer open your mail. They will notice the next time they try to open it.
The company's page does not say whether the other person is told about this change.
Sam loses access to the things you shared, like content and benefits, so they may notice when they shop or watch.
Riley may notice that they can no longer shop from your account after you remove them.
Sam, your Echo Dot no longer shows your account's content. Whoever uses it will notice right away because it's been deregistered.
When you leave Sam's family group, the things you shared through the family group will no longer be available to Sam. Sam may notice when those things stop working.
Google sends Riley an email saying Riley was removed.
The other person can no longer see the photos you shared with them. They may notice when they look at the photos next time.

handRead.by: the AI coding assistant that built Spare Key, reading all 54 notices for who is who
handRead.which: maps.sharing.link runs 1 and 3 (the person’s location described as the other person’s), amazon.device.other run 3 (speaks to Sam), google.apps.location run 3 (the app "may notice")
handRead.note: Three code checks for these were added after reading this run and applied to the same saved answers; a fresh run is the honest test of them.
